jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Careers that make a difference

We work to build and maintain an accountable government that motivates, inspires, and provides opportunities for Vuntut Gwitchin Citizens. Our employees have the opportunity to make meaningful connections and work on initiatives that make a real difference in people’s lives.

“With boundless pride in our ancient cultural heritage and ancestral homelands, we exercise our inherent right to self-government, to take the responsibility for the general welfare of our Citizens, and to provide for the good government of our community, lands and resources.”

—Preamble, VGFN Constitution

About The Role

The Executive Director is the senior administrative leader of the Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation (VGFN) and is responsible for the effective administration, management and day-to-day operations of the government. The Executive Director translates the priorities and directives approved by Chief and Council into operational plans, budgets, policies, programs and services. The position ensures that VGFN resources are managed responsibly, employees are effectively supported and supervised, and operations are carried out in accordance with VGFN laws, policies, approved budgets and applicable legislation and agreements. Reporting to the Chief, some of the responsibilities of the position include but are not limited to;

Administration and Operational Leadership
- Leads and oversees VGFN’s day-to-day administration and operations, establishes departmental priorities and performance expectations, and ensures Chief and Council directives and strategic priorities are effectively implemented.

People Management and Human Resources
- Provides leadership, supervision, coaching and performance management to Directors and Managers while overseeing recruitment, employee relations, labour relations, staff development and the implementation of HR policies and practices.

Financial Management and Resource Stewardship
- Leads organizational budgeting and financial planning, monitors financial performance and expenditures, oversees procurement and contract administration, and ensures responsible and accountable use of VGFN resources.

Program and Service Delivery
- Oversees the administration and delivery of VGFN programs and services, ensuring departmental plans, service standards and performance measures align with approved priorities and available resources.

Policy, Compliance and Corporate Governance Administration
- Leads the development, implementation and maintenance of organizational policies, procedures and administrative systems while ensuring compliance with VGFN governance frameworks, agreements, applicable legislation and regulatory requirements.

Management Committee and Organizational Planning
- Chairs and leads the Management Committee, coordinates departmental planning and resource allocation, monitors organizational performance, and provides regular operational updates and recommendations to Chief and Council.

Communications and Stakeholder Coordination
- Ensures effective internal and external communication on administrative and operational matters, coordinates relationships with stakeholders and service providers, and works with the Political & Governance Affairs Director to align political commitments with operational implementation.

Emergency and Business Continuity Management
- Oversees administrative emergency response, business continuity and employee safety arrangements, ensuring organizational readiness and coordinated operational responses to emergencies.

What We Offer

Working Hours: 80 hours bi-weekly.
4% Northern Community Remoteness Allowance for employees residing in Old Crow full-time.
4% Northern Travel Allowance for employees residing in Old Crow full-time.
4 weeks’ vacation to start plus two weeks paid time off over the Christmas season.
A very healthy extended benefits package.
12 days management leave per year
10 days sick pay per year.
10 days paid special/personal leave per year.
A matched pension plan.
Subsidized Housing may be available.
Relocation Allowance.

‍

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in business, management, public administration, Indigenous governance or related field, as well as continued personal and professional development. A professional designation is an asset.

Significant (15+ years) leadership experience developing, implementing, and evaluating organizational strategic visions.
Considerable (10+ years) experience motivating and managing staff, overseeing finance (budgets and procurement), policy, and governance, to translate political direction into operational strategy and business plans.
Considerable experience in stakeholder management and negotiations to navigate and advance organizational political positions and interests.
Leadership experience in the public sector and/or an Indigenous organization possessing a final/self-governing agreement is an asset.

‍

Supporting You Along The Way

We believe that a rewarding career is not only good for our employees, but it also leads to better outcomes for our clients, workplace and the community. That’s why we are committed to providing you with a competitive salary, health benefits, and a retirement plan. Beyond compensation, you will have the opportunity to make meaningful connections and work on initiatives that make a real difference in people’s lives.

‍

To Apply

Please send your resume and a cover letter to: jobs@vgfn.ca. In accordance with the Canadian Human Rights Act (CHRA, Section 16(1)), hiring preference will be given to Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation Citizens. Following this, preference will be extended to Indigenous candidates, and then to those with experience and knowledge of First Nations customs and practices.

‍

❖ While we appreciate all applications, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

‍

Job Description & Summary

At PwC, our people in tax services focus on providing advice and guidance to clients on tax planning, compliance, and strategy. These individuals help businesses navigate complex tax regulations and optimize their tax positions.

In tax accounting services at PwC, you will assist businesses in preparing and reviewing tax provisions, tax returns, and financial statements, confirming compliance with accounting standards and tax regulations.

The opportunity

  As a Financial Reporting and Tax Compliance Director, you'll work as part of a team of problem solvers,          helping to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution. Responsibilities level include but are not limited to:   

Support team to disrupt, improve and evolve ways of working when necessary  

Managing a variety of projects, including compilations, review engagements, and tax compliance engagements  

Being the right-hand of our local partners    

Arrange and sponsor appropriate assignments and experiences to help people realize their potential and support their long-term aspirations  

Identify gaps in the market and spot opportunities to create value propositions  

Look for opportunities to scale efficiencies and new ways of working across multiple projects and environments  

Create an environment where people and technology thrive together to accomplish more than they could apart  

Promote and encourage others to value differences when working in diverse teams  

Drive and take ownership for developing connections that help deliver what is best for our people and stakeholders  

Influence and facilitate the creation of long-term relationships which add value to the firm

Uphold the firm's code of ethics and business conduct    

What you’ll bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here's what we look for:  

Bachelor's in accounting or in any related field  

Canadian CPA Designation or CPA Audito r and between 8-10 years' experience in a similar rol e in an accounting firm  

Ability to coach junior staff members and being present in the local market  

Detailed knowledge and understanding of Accounting Standards for Private Entities (ASPE), CSRS 4200 Compilation engagements, CSRE 2400 Review engagements, Canadian Audit Standards    

Strong communication , and facilitator skills with demonstrated ability to work with multiple personalitie s  

Exceptional interpersonal, communication, listening and coaching skills  

Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage multiple assignments in an organized manner  

Strong analytical capability, sound business sense and creative mind that have earned you a reputation of providing excellence in client service  

The successful candidate requires fluency in English, in addition to French as they will be required to support or collaborate with English-speaking clients, colleagues and/or stakeholders during the course of their employment with PwC Canada  

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.  

The salary range for this position is $ 133 , 1 00 - $ 1 83 , 1 00. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres . Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements .  We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.   

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc  

PwC Canada acknowledges that we work and live across Turtle Island, on the land that is now known as Canada, which are the lands of the ancestral, treaty and unceded territories of the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples. We recognize the systemic racism, colonialism and oppression that Indigenous Peoples have experienced and still go through, and we commit to allyship and solidarity.

The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruiting is just getting started, so we know you have questions about how and why we use it. At certain points during our recruiting process, we rely on AI to improve your experience. This could be during resume review or curating personalized job recommendations, asking you clarifying questions via a chatbot or during our interview scheduling to improve your experience. Our use of AI helps ensure we combat bias by evaluating candidates equally and fairly, without seeing identity information, such as your name, or gender for example). AI also helps us better predict successful hires by reviewing all applicants for a role and the relationship between your skills, experience and likely success at PwC Canada. While AI supports parts of our recruitment process, final hiring decisions always involve human review. For more information about our use and protection of your data, please refer to our Privacy Policy (https://www.pwc.com/ca/en/privacy-policy.html).

L’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans le domaine du recrutement en est à ses balbutiements. Nous savons que vous pourriez vous demander comment et pourquoi nous y avons recours. À certains stades de notre processus de recrutement, nous comptons sur l’IA pour améliorer votre expérience. Par exemple, pendant l’examen du curriculum vitæ ou l’élaboration d’une liste de recommandations personnalisées, un agent conversationnel pourrait vous demander des précisions ou fixer avec vous un rendez-vous pour l’entrevue. L’IA nous aide à mieux lutter contre les préjugés, car l’évaluation des candidats se fait de façon juste et équitable, sans que les informations d’identification comme le nom ou le sexe soient connues. Elle nous permet également de mieux repérer les bons candidats pour un poste et d’évaluer le lien entre leurs compétences, leur expérience et leurs chances de réussir chez PwC Canada. Bien que l’IA facilite certaines étapes de notre processus de recrutement, les décisions finales d’embauche sont toujours prises par des personnes. Pour en savoir plus sur l’utilisation et la protection de vos données personnelles, consultez notre politique sur la protection des renseignements confidentiels (https://www.pwc.com/ca/fr/privacy-policy.html).

jobs.title: Customer Success Director
jobs.description:
This employer is an HR technology company seeking a Director of Customer Success Managers to own gross retention and net revenue retention across its named and higher-value accounts. Reporting to the VP of Global Customer Success, you will lead a global organisation of managers and customer success managers who protect the customer base, manage renewals and drive expansion.

The Role

• Lead, hire and coach managers of customer success across multiple regions and time zones.
• Set and manage coverage models by account tier, own the annual re-tiering of books and standardise tier-specific playbooks.
• Oversee renewals across the portfolio and move legacy evergreen agreements to standard contractual terms.
• Lead the weekly and monthly risk and churn review with revenue leadership, keeping real-time health signals and remediation plans for at-risk accounts.
• Set rules of engagement with account management, and report retention, net revenue retention and portfolio risk to executive leadership.

What You'll Need

• 10+ years of experience in customer success or account management within B2B SaaS or global services, including 5+ years leading people managers.
• A proven record of protecting and expanding a large customer book with measurable gains in gross and net retention.
• Experience leading distributed teams across regions and designing tiered coverage models, playbooks and scalable operating frameworks.
• Strong executive presence and fluency with Salesforce and customer health data platforms; HR tech, payroll or global expansion experience is preferred.

What's On Offer

• Annual fixed pay of CAD 140,000 – CAD 175,000, plus variable compensation tied to retention.
• Medical, dental and vision insurance, spending accounts, generous paid parental leave and flexible time off.
• A remote-first team, with a sabbatical after five years.

Apply via Haystack today!
